International News · 16 Sources · 4 Regions

Daily Brief

France braces for a second weekend of mass protests over the cost of living, with 70,000 police deployed nationwide and major Paris museums closed after last week's riots caused hundreds of millions of euros in damage [BBC, RFI, France 24]. The situation was further inflamed by a deadly terrorist shooting west of Paris on Friday that killed one person and wounded five, which President Macron called 'a racist terrorist attack' targeting people of migrant origin [BBC, RFI]. In US-Canada relations, the Trump administration announced selective tariff relief on Canadian goods ahead of the midterm elections, a move tied to Republican Senator Susan Collins' tight re-election race in Maine [BBC, Le Monde]. Serbia heads to polls Sunday in what may be the most significant challenge to President Vučić's 12-year rule, driven by a student protest movement that emerged from anti-corruption demonstrations following the deadly Novi Sad station collapse [BBC]. Meanwhile, health officials are racing to contain an Ebola outbreak that has now spread to four African countries, with Nigeria confirming its first case and investigators struggling to determine the chain of transmission [Guardian].

France Deploys 70,000 Police as Nation Braces for Second Weekend of Mass Protests

  • France has mobilized 70,000 police officers and gendarmes nationwide, with helicopters, armored vehicles, and water cannons deployed ahead of Saturday protests over cost of living
  • Major Paris museums including the Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, and Picasso Museum closed for the day; Art Basel Paris cancelled its weekend program

Deadly Shooting West of Paris Labeled 'Racist Terrorist Attack' by French Authorities

  • One person killed and five wounded, including a 12-year-old girl shot eight times, in drive-by shooting across two Paris suburbs (Trappes and La Verrière)
  • Suspect, a 39-year-old man, arrested and found with rigged gas cylinders in his home; used military-grade automatic weapon
  • President Macron called it 'a turning point in the life of our Republic' and the first random racial killing of its kind in France
  • Targets appeared to be people of migrant origin at multiple locations including a petrol station, health center, and playground

Trump Administration Lifts Some Canada Tariffs Two Weeks Before Midterm Elections

  • White House announced tariff relief on Canadian goods including plywood, paper products, machinery, and refrigeration equipment effective October 30
  • Republican Senator Susan Collins, in tight Maine re-election race, announced the exemptions first, saying she lobbied for changes to help state agriculture
  • US had imposed 50% levy on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods after trade talks collapsed in August
  • While some tariffs lifted, new tariffs introduced on other items including carpets and waste products
